correctness.rationale: Given I, its horizontal projection T and central intersection K determine I as the inverse image of a unique graph in T direct-sum Z/K. Products ignore all central parts, so the sole closure condition is that K contain the spans TJ+JT; graphs then number q^{d(ac-e)}. For any fixed X component of T, varying the opposite block realizes every map W -> im(X); for any Y, the opposite products realize all maps with rows in its row space. Spanning these gives the exact L tensor W* and U tensor R spaces even when the two coordinates of T are linked. Choosing complements shows their intersection is L tensor R, giving h=cℓ+ar-ℓr. Containing K are counted in the quotient by this sum. The d-subspaces with support at most (L',R') lie in a b(i+j)-space, so product-lattice Möbius inversion yields the displayed M_d with both codimension exponents, and weighting the unique choices proves the full polynomial, including zero and full ideals. No use of characteristic zero or division by 2 occurs. An independently written RREF and matrix-unit ideal-closure test (`python3 /tmp/opencode/frozen_checks.py ideal`) confirmed the two (1,2,1) tests over fields of size 2 and 3 and fully enumerated (2,2,1) at q=2, agreeing with all nine coefficients and total 2859. The frozen q=3 size-eight example is formula evaluation, not a direct enumeration; the all-field proof controls it. Frozen checker and recorded output were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The embedded ideal polynomial is a complete dimension invariant for a natural family of finite radicals. It sees the extra flexibility from a larger middle block, including linked non-coordinate subspaces, without classifying every ambient subspace afresh. The closed finite-field census is distinct from unital parabolic ideals, all subalgebras and integral local ideal-growth formulas, and supplies every quotient-size count at every allowed block shape.
